name: Sweden
tagline: Free for EU students, but few bachelor's are in English
summary: Sweden has one national application portal, one national ranking system, and no tuition fees for EU/EEA citizens. Your IB total is converted to a Swedish merit value on a published table, and that number alone decides most places - there is no personal statement and usually no interview. The catch is supply and timing: most Swedish bachelor's degrees are taught in Swedish, and University Admissions tells IB students who have not yet finished the Diploma to apply in the second round, which closes on 15 April 2027.
whyConsider: No tuition fee at all if you are an EU/EEA or Swiss citizen.
One application at universityadmissions.se covers every Swedish university.
Your IB points convert to a Swedish merit value on a published, public table - you can work out your own score before you apply.
If you take Swedish, Danish or Norwegian Language A and reach grade 4 or higher, you already meet the Swedish-language entry requirement, which opens Swedish-taught programmes too.
Admission is score-based and transparent: no essays, no references, no interview for most programmes.
watchOuts: English-taught bachelor's degrees are genuinely scarce. Lund lists ten, KTH lists one. Most English teaching in Sweden is at master's level.

You almost certainly cannot use the January round. University Admissions says applicants without a completed IB Diploma should not apply to the first round, so a May 2027 candidate applies in round two (deadline 15 April 2027) - where some English-taught programmes are no longer open. Stockholm School of Economics is the exception: it runs its own January process and admits on predicted grades.
Housing is a queue system you join years in advance in Stockholm. Register the day you decide Sweden is on your list.
Non-EU students: from 11 June 2026 a study residence permit limits you to 15 hours of paid work per week, and new rules also tighten study-progress requirements.
Stockholm School of Economics also demands an SAT, ACT or ITB-Business score on top of the IB - that is unusual for Sweden and needs a year's notice.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: No national minimum points figure is published. A full IB Diploma awarded 2021 or later gives general eligibility (grundlaggande behorighet) in its own right; individual Course Results do not.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Specific entry requirements are met subject by subject. Minimum IB grade 4 is normally required, with grade 3 accepted for Biology, Chemistry and Physics at HL and, for a lower-level Swedish course, in some Mathematics courses. Published maths mapping: Mathematics: applications and interpretation SL maps to Swedish Matematik 3c; Mathematics: analysis and approaches SL maps to Matematik 4; Mathematics: applications and interpretation HL maps to Matematik 5; Mathematics: analysis and approaches HL maps to Matematik specialisering. Sciences: Physics/Chemistry/Biology SL or HL map to Fysik 2 / Kemi 2 / Biologi 2. History SL/HL maps to Historia 1b; the IB Diploma itself covers Samhallskunskap 1b; Economics or Global politics SL/HL maps to Samhallskunskap 2.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: UHR publishes a fixed conversion table from IB total points to the Swedish merit value (meritvarde) on the 10.00-20.00 scale: 24 = 13.18, 25 = 13.94, 26 = 14.62, 27 = 15.21, 28 = 15.76, 29 = 16.26, 30 = 16.70, 31 = 17.11, 32 = 17.53, 33 = 17.92, 34 = 18.25, 35 = 18.57, 36 = 18.88, 37 = 19.17, 38 = 19.38, 39 = 19.54, 40 = 19.70, 41 = 19.79, 42 = 19.90, 43-45 = 20.00. Up to 2.5 extra merit points (meritpoang) can be added for qualifying courses in modern languages, English and mathematics taken outside the Diploma.
notes: IB English A (HL or SL), English B HL, and English B SL taught in English all meet the higher Swedish English 7 requirement. English B SL taught in a language other than English meets English 6, which is the level needed for general eligibility.

The Swedish-language requirement for Swedish-taught programmes can be met with Language and Literature A or Literature A in Swedish, Danish or Norwegian at HL or SL with grade 4 or higher. Danish A counts.

IB applicants sit in selection group BI if eligible on the Diploma alone. They move into BII if they add Swedish upper-secondary or adult-education courses afterwards. If you retake IB exams you are ranked in BI on the original score and in BII on the improved one.

You raise your IB total only by retaking IB exams. Swedish upper-secondary or komvux courses are added to your merit value only when they complete a missing entry requirement or earn merit points; they do not replace IB grades.

For a May session, ask your IB coordinator to release results to UHR through the IB Result Service (recipient code "UHR"). University Admissions' 2027 dates give IB students completing this spring until 5 July 2027 to document their completed studies in the second round.
Rules differ by award year. The 2021-and-later ruleset is the one that applies to a May 2027 Diploma.

deadlines.label: First admission round opens (autumn 2027)
deadlines.notes: This is the round aimed at international applicants. Most English-taught programmes are only offered here.

deadlines.label: First admission round application deadline
deadlines.notes: Closes at midnight CET, and it is also the ranking deadline. University Admissions' IB guidance page says "If you haven't yet completed your IB Diploma programme, do not apply to the first admissions round", because University Admissions "will not be able to evaluate your application in time for admissions decisions in late March/April" without a completed transcript and diploma (https://www.universityadmissions.se/en/apply-to-bachelors/provide-application-documents-bachelors/ib-studies/). A May 2027 candidate therefore normally cannot use this round — the second round, below, is yours.

deadlines.label: First round — supporting documents, and your proof of fee exemption
deadlines.notes: One day, three things. As an EU/EEA citizen you pay no application fee and no tuition, but you do not get the exemption automatically — you have to document your EU/EEA citizenship by this date, and University Admissions handles that on the same deadline it uses to collect the fee from everyone else. All supporting materials are due the same day.

deadlines.label: Second admission round opens
deadlines.notes: This is the realistic round for a May 2027 IB candidate. Fewer English-taught programmes are open here.

deadlines.label: First round bachelor's results
deadlines.notes: Bachelor's results. Master's results come a week earlier, on 1 April — that date is context here rather than a milestone of its own, because nothing on this profile is a master's application. If you applied in this round at all, this is your day.

deadlines.label: Second admission round application deadline
deadlines.notes: Also the final ranking day: the order you put your choices in on this date is the order that is used. The fee-exemption date (23 April), the document date (21 June) and the IB results date (5 July) are entries of their own.

deadlines.label: Second round — document your fee-exempt status
deadlines.notes: Eight days after you apply, and easy to miss because it lands after the part that feels like the deadline. As an EU/EEA citizen you are exempt from the application fee and from tuition, but you must document that exemption by this date; non-EU/EEA applicants pay the fee by the same date. An application whose exemption is not documented is not processed.

deadlines.label: Second round supporting documents deadline
deadlines.notes: The general document deadline for the second round. It is not the date for your IB results: University Admissions gives IB students completing their studies this spring until 5 July 2027 for that (next entry). Anything else you need - an ID copy, other transcripts - goes in by 21 June, and University Admissions asks you to upload documents you already have with the application.

deadlines.label: Second round — IB results must reach University Admissions
deadlines.notes: Published on the autumn 2027 key-dates page: applicants completing an IB/EB programme this spring "have until 5 July to submit documentation of your completed upper secondary studies". For a May 2027 Diploma that means your coordinator releasing your results to recipient code "UHR" through the IB Result Service. The site's own calendar has IB results day on 6 July 2027; if the IB publishes on the 6th, ask University Admissions how a result released after this date is handled.

deadlines.label: Second round results published
deadlines.notes: The first notification of selection results for the round a May 2027 IB candidate actually uses. What you must do next has its own entry, one week later, and it is the date on this page most worth putting in a calendar now.

deadlines.label: Reply to your second-round offer
deadlines.notes: You have seven days from the 9 July notification to reply, and a place you do not reply to is a place you lose — including a place you have been offered while still waiting on a higher choice. Set this one before you apply, not after you are offered.

deadlines.label: Second notification of selection results
deadlines.notes: This is where a place you were waiting on can arrive, after the 16 July replies have cleared the lists. No reply is required to this notification — which is precisely why it must not be confused with the 9 July one, where a reply is required.

deadlines.label: Semester start
deadlines.notes: Date given by Stockholm University; other universities start in late August or early September.

steps: Work out your likely merit value from the UHR conversion table before you shortlist anything, because that number is what actually decides your place.
Check each programme's specific entry requirements and match them against your IB subjects and grades - grade 4 is the normal minimum, grade 3 for HL sciences.
Create an account at universityadmissions.se and rank up to a set number of programme choices in order of preference. Your ranking matters: you are only offered your highest-ranked eligible choice.
Upload your IB transcripts and, if you are an EU/EEA citizen, proof of citizenship so you are exempted from the 900 SEK application fee.
Ask your IB Diploma Programme coordinator to send your final results directly to UHR through the IB Result Service.
Reply to your offer by the stated date or you lose the place - Sweden is strict about this.
Register in a student housing queue in your target city as early as you possibly can, independently of the application itself.
application.selectionNotes: Selection is almost entirely by number. A third or more of places on each programme go to the grade groups (BI/BII), where you are ranked on your converted merit value, and a further share goes to applicants ranked on the Swedish national aptitude test (hogskoleprovet), which is sat in Swedish. IB students normally compete in BI. A small number of programmes - art, design, music, architecture - add portfolios or auditions, and Stockholm School of Economics requires an SAT, ACT or ITB-Business score.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Limited but real. Lund and Gothenburg each list ten English-taught bachelor's programmes, Uppsala eight, Stockholm and Jonkoping seven, Malmo six, Umea and Lulea four; KTH, Linkoping, Karolinska and SLU one each, and Chalmers none. Most Swedish bachelor's degrees are taught in Swedish; English dominates at master's level.
language.englishProof: You need Swedish English 6 / English Level 2. An IB English A (HL or SL), English B HL, or English B SL taught in English exceeds this and meets the higher English 7. English B SL taught in another language meets English 6. Without an IB English course, IELTS Academic 6.5 with no section below 5.5, or TOEFL iBT total 90 with 20 in writing (for results up to 20 January 2026) / total 4.5 on the new 1-6 scale with no section below 4 (for results from 21 January 2026), are accepted.
notes: Swedish-taught programmes need Swedish 3 level. Swedish, Danish or Norwegian Language A or Literature A at HL or SL with grade 4 satisfies it, which is a real advantage if you take one of them.
The national aptitude test (hogskoleprovet), which fills part of every programme's intake, is only available in Swedish.
Everyday life in Swedish cities runs comfortably in English, but municipal paperwork does not always.

tuitionEuEea.value: No tuition fee. Citizens of the EU, EEA and Switzerland are exempt from both the application fee and tuition, but must document their citizenship to get the exemption.

tuitionNonEu.value: Set by each university. Uppsala University states 49,500-90,000 SEK per semester of full-time study, i.e. roughly 99,000-180,000 SEK per year (about EUR 8,800-16,000 at 11.2750 SEK/EUR). Fees vary widely by subject and institution.
tuitionNonEu.year: Uppsala page last updated 9 October 2025; the page does not state an entry year - re-check for 2027 entry

costs.applicationFee: 900 SEK (about EUR 80) per semester applied for, regardless of how many programmes you choose. EU/EEA/Swiss citizens are exempt.

livingCostMonthly.value: Lund University's own student budget: food 3,000 SEK, accommodation 4,000-8,000 SEK, course literature 400-1,000 SEK, other 1,500 SEK - roughly 8,900-12,500 SEK per month (about EUR 790-1,110). Swedish students on full state loans and grants receive roughly 9,000-12,000 SEK per month.

notes: Non-EU students applying for a study residence permit must show at least 10,656 SEK per month (about EUR 945) for the whole permit period if applying in 2026; the 2025 figure was 10,584 SEK. The amount is reset each year.
The study residence permit application itself costs 1,500 SEK (about EUR 133) for adults.
Euro conversions use the ECB reference rate of 11.2750 SEK per EUR on 21 September 2026 and will drift.

funding.note: Because Sweden is a Nordic country, it is paid as if you studied in Denmark — for anyone starting after 1 July 2025, for the programme's prescribed length only.

funding: CSN (the Swedish student finance agency) is the route for those with a settled connection to Sweden; eligibility for an EU citizen who moves purely to study is restricted and must be checked directly with CSN.
Swedish Institute scholarships and individual university scholarships exist mainly for fee-paying non-EU/EEA students. Bachelor-level availability is limited - check each university.
Because there is no tuition fee for EU/EEA citizens, the real cost question in Sweden is rent, not fees.
workRights: EU/EEA citizens can work without restriction alongside study. Non-EU students on a study residence permit granted on or after 11 June 2026 may work a maximum of 15 hours per week. Source: https://www.migrationsverket.se/en/you-want-to-apply/study/higher-education.html
residency: As an EU/EEA citizen you do not need a residence permit for Sweden - you have a right of residence as a student. In practice you register with Skatteverket to get a personnummer, which you need for almost everything from a bank account to a doctor's appointment, and that normally requires an intended stay of at least 12 months. Non-EU citizens must apply to Migrationsverket for a residence permit for higher education studies, showing admission, health insurance for courses under a year, and at least 10,656 SEK per month (2026 figure) for the permit period; the fee is 1,500 SEK.
housing: Not allocated by the universities. Each city has its own student housing foundation with a credit-day queue - SSSB in Stockholm, AF Bostader and LU Accommodation in Lund, SGS in Gothenburg, Uppsalahem in Uppsala. You earn one credit day per day in the queue, so joining early is the whole game; SSSB waits are commonly quoted in the hundreds of days. Most large universities give no housing guarantee. Register in the queue as soon as a city is on your shortlist, well before you apply.
healthcare: As an EU/EEA citizen, carry your European Health Insurance Card for necessary care. Once you register with Skatteverket and get a personnummer you use the normal Swedish system with the usual patient fees. Non-EU students must hold comprehensive health insurance for studies under one year; for longer permits they are normally covered once registered.

institutions.name: Lund University
institutions.englishBachelors: Ten English-taught bachelor's programmes open to international students
institutions.note: A large university about 45 minutes from Copenhagen by train, with ten English-taught bachelor's programmes open to international students.

institutions.name: Uppsala University
institutions.englishBachelors: Eight international bachelor's programmes, in Uppsala and at Campus Gotland in Visby
institutions.note: Founded in 1477, with a student-nation social life that is unlike anywhere else in Scandinavia.

institutions.name: Stockholm University
institutions.englishBachelors: Seven, including International Business and Politics; Business, Ethics and Sustainability; two Latin American Studies tracks; Political Science and Regional Studies; and Middle Eastern and North African Studies
institutions.note: Strong in social sciences and sits inside a national park in the middle of the capital. Seven bachelor's programmes are taught in English; the rest are in Swedish.

institutions.name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: One: BSc Information and Communication Technology
institutions.note: A technical university, but at bachelor level it teaches in English on exactly one programme: Information and Communication Technology.

institutions.name: Chalmers University of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: None. Chalmers states that all its bachelor's programmes are taught in Swedish (only the fifth semester is in English); its master's programmes are in English.
institutions.note: Sweden's other big engineering school, closely tied to Gothenburg's automotive and maritime industries. Its bachelor's degrees are in Swedish and need Swedish 3 - which Swedish, Danish or Norwegian A at grade 4 or higher meets.

institutions.name: University of Gothenburg
institutions.englishBachelors: Ten international bachelor's programmes, including Business and Economics, International Relations, Software Engineering and Management, Computer Science and AI, and several in craft, design and music
institutions.note: A broad university spread across Sweden's second city, with unusually strong art and design schools attached.

institutions.name: Stockholm School of Economics
institutions.englishBachelors: Two: Business and Economics, and Retail Management
institutions.note: Small, private and very selective: it asks for at least 31 IB points but says 39 or above is usually needed, plus an SAT of 1300, ACT 28 or ITB-Business 112. Unlike the rest of Sweden it admits on predicted grades in January: apply on universityadmissions.se and on SSE's own portal by 15 January 2027.
institutions.ibPageNote: Checked 2026-09-23. The international-applicant page states the IB requirement plainly: an IB score of 31 out of 45 is the requirement, with English B SL and Mathematics Applications and Interpretation SL passed, plus a university admission test; it adds that 39 or above is usually needed in practice.

institutions.name: Jonkoping University
institutions.englishBachelors: Seven: International Economics, International Management, International Marketing, Sustainable Supply Chain Management, Graphic Design and Web Development, Mechanical Engineering, and Prosthetics and Orthotics
institutions.note: A smaller foundation university in a lakeside town that punches above its weight on English-taught bachelor's, especially through its international business school. Its own JU Direct application opens on 16 October 2026 and admits on a rolling basis.

institutions.name: Linkoping University
institutions.englishBachelors: One international bachelor's programme taught in English, per Linkoping's own page
institutions.note: Known for problem-based, project-heavy teaching and a campus culture built around student-run engineering work.

institutions.name: Umea University
institutions.englishBachelors: Four bachelor's programmes, all taught in English
institutions.note: Far north, dark in winter, and home to an industrial design school; four of its bachelor's programmes are taught in English.

institutions.name: Malmo University
institutions.englishBachelors: Six: European Studies, Human Rights, Interaction Design, International Migration and Ethnic Relations, International Relations, and Peace and Conflict Studies
institutions.note: Twenty minutes over the bridge from Copenhagen, young, practical and very international in outlook.

institutions.name: Lulea University of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Four: Computer Graphics for Games and Film, Computer Game Development and Programming, Mineral Resource Engineering, and Music
institutions.note: Arctic-adjacent technical university with a space campus in Kiruna and close ties to Sweden's heavy industry.

institutions.name: Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: One: Forest and Landscape, taught in Alnarp, near Malmo and Lund
institutions.note: The place to look if you want animals, forests, food systems or landscape rather than a conventional science degree.

institutions.name: Karolinska Institutet
institutions.englishBachelors: One: the Bachelor's Programme in Biomedicine, taught in English on the Solna campus
institutions.note: World-famous for medical research and it awards the Nobel Prize in Medicine. Its one English-taught bachelor's is Biomedicine; its other bachelor's degrees, including medicine and nursing, are taught in Swedish.
